content.value_statement: Trading strategy tests often overstate performance because they ignore bias, costs, and validation discipline. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through robust backtesting patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains event-driven and vectorized backtester structures for trading strategies.
Shows how to avoid look-ahead bias by shifting signals and using point-in-time data.
Provides walk-forward optimization patterns with training and test windows.
Includes transaction cost, slippage, drawdown, and risk-adjusted return calculations.
Demonstrates Monte Carlo analysis for drawdown and loss probability estimates.
limitations: It is guidance and example code, not a complete production trading platform.
It does not provide market data, broker integration, or live execution.
Examples require review before use with real capital or regulated workflows.
Statistical outputs depend on data quality and strategy assumptions.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Strategy Backtest
use_cases.description: Create a first backtest with realistic costs, shifted signals, and basic performance metrics.

use_cases.title: Review Backtest Methodology
use_cases.description: Check an existing test for look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, overfitting, and missing cost assumptions.

use_cases.title: Build Validation Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Design walk-forward testing, parameter selection, and Monte Carlo robustness checks for research pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Backtest
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backtesting-frameworks skill to outline a simple daily trading backtest. Include data needs, signal timing, costs, and core metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Find Bias Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backtest design for look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, overfitting, and transaction cost gaps. List fixes in priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Design Walk-Forward Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a walk-forward optimization plan for this strategy. Define train windows, test windows, parameter grids, and acceptance metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Add Robustness Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this backtesting workflow with Monte Carlo analysis, drawdown distributions, loss probabilities, and reporting thresholds for investment review.

output_examples.input: Review a momentum strategy backtest for common flaws.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering signal lag, out-of-sample testing, transaction costs, survivorship controls, and metrics that need recalculation.
A testing plan with rolling windows, parameter selection rules, validation metrics, and a summary of expected robustness checks.

output_examples.input: Explain which performance metrics to report.
output_examples.output: A concise metric set covering total return, annual return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, Calmar ratio, drawdown, win rate, and profit factor.

best_practices: Use point-in-time data and shift signals before measuring returns.
Model commissions, slippage, market impact, and realistic execution timing.
Reserve out-of-sample data and use walk-forward testing before comparing strategies.
anti_patterns: Optimizing parameters on the full history and reporting the same period as final performance.
Ignoring delisted securities, data adjustments, missing data, and transaction costs.
Treating high Sharpe ratios as reliable without drawdown, capacity, and robustness checks.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It provides backtesting guidance and examples. It does not connect to brokers or execute orders.

faq.question: Can it help prevent look-ahead bias?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes point-in-time data, shifted signals, and strict train, validation, and test separation.

faq.question: Does it include transaction cost modeling?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include commissions, slippage, and realistic execution assumptions.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it enough for regulated investment use?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as engineering guidance. Legal, compliance, and model risk review remain necessary.

faq.question: What data does it require?
faq.answer: It expects historical market data with reliable timestamps. OHLCV data is enough for many examples.
